meeting_header:
Date: 2025-10-22
Time: 16:00 UTC
Duration: 42 minutes
Attendees: Jordan Lee (Redwood AE), Priya Nair (Redwood SE), Marta Ruiz (Helix Head of AI), Samir Kapoor (Helix Platform Eng), Lena Cho (Helix Product)
summary: Intro demo of Redwood's Eval/Quality monitoring features (called internally 'Quality Watchtower' for this deck). Covered prompt set management, regression alerts, A/B/traffic split comparisons, and quick API/Console walkthrough. Customer cares about reproducible regression detection, traffic split experiments, and security controls (VPC, SOC2, KMS). Agreed to run a short A/B benchmark and share security docs; potential dedicated pilot pending benchmark results.
transcript:
[00:00] Jordan Lee: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. I'm Jordan from Redwood Inference, AE on the Helix account. With me is Priya Nair, our solutions engineer.
[00:14] Marta Ruiz: Hi, Marta here — head of AI. Quick note, Samir's on for platform questions, Lena for product.
[00:21] Priya Nair: Great, we'll run through a demo of what we call the Quality Watchtower — prompt sets, regression alerting, and then a live A slash B traffic split compare in the console and via API.
[00:35] Samir Kapoor: Quick ask up front — latency targets for us are 150ms 95th when calls are regional, and we'd like to see token cost impact of batching. Also must be VPC-friendly.
[00:46] Jordan Lee: Yep totally understood. We'll call out Hosted vs Dedicated tradeoffs, and show estimates in the Optimize tab.
[00:58] Priya Nair: Alright opening the console — bear with me, the screen may be a little fuzzy, I'm on a hotel wifi. So first, prompt sets. You can group prompts into suites, label expected outputs and measurement metrics, and attach baseline references.
[01:20] Lena Cho: When you say baseline, is that a saved model version?
[01:25] Priya Nair: Exactly, you pin a model and snapshot prompt responses. Then we run regression checks on new model rollouts or config changes. The automatic drift check is out of the box but you can refine thresholds.
[01:39] Marta Ruiz: How frequently do regression alerts fire? We have daily runs and we don't want noise.
[01:45] Priya Nair: Default is daily aggregated checks, but you can set sliding windows and sensitivity. Also we support pairwise comparisons so you can see if a change actually improves a metric like factuality or safety score.
[01:58] Jordan Lee: Will note, the pairwise is helpful for A/B because it shows distribution shift and delta per metric.
[02:06] Samir Kapoor: Are metrics computed on-host or do we have to ship logs out?
[02:11] Priya Nair: Metrics are computed within your chosen deployment — for Redwood Private the telemetry can stay in your VPC. For hosted, telemetry goes to Redwood's managed eval pipeline but can be set to mask PII.
[02:26] Marta Ruiz: Do you support KMS/HSM integrations for embeddings and logs?
[02:31] Jordan Lee: Yes, we have KMS integration and can route keys via customer KMS for Dedicated and Private. For hosted, we offer customer-managed keys in certain regions.
[02:43] Lena Cho: Show us an A/B setup.
[02:46] Priya Nair: Sure, switching to traffic experiments. You define split percentages, assign model variants (for example, model-v1 on quantized path vs model-v2 full FP16). We'll demo a 50/50.
[02:58] [screening delay] Priya Nair: Loading the run — note this dataset is a small sample of Helix prompts you shared last week, we anonymized a few fields.
[03:13] Jordan Lee: One thing to call out, our continuous batching can reduce per-token cost but it increases tail latency slightly; the console shows expected cost and latency changes per bucket.
[03:27] Samir Kapoor: Could you quantify that? Like percent increase at 95th?
[03:31] Priya Nair: Typical is 5–12% P95 increase when batch windows widen, but token cost drops can be 20–40% depending on reuse and KV cache hit rate. Your traffic profile will determine the sweet spot.
[03:50] Marta Ruiz: KV cash?
[03:51] Priya Nair: Sorry, KV cache — my bad.
[03:54] Lena Cho: There's often mis-transcriptions in these calls — noted.
[04:00] Jordan Lee: On the API side, endpoints for the eval suite allow you to POST a prompt set and get scored responses back, we support streaming responses and structured function outputs as well.
[04:14] Samir Kapoor: For their nightly batch, how would we run an automated regression alert?
[04:18] Priya Nair: You set a baseline snapshot, schedule a run or hook the webhook into your CI. If the delta exceeds thresholds, the alert creates a ticket and emails a distribution list. You can also automatically rollback traffic using the canary policy.
[04:36] Marta Ruiz: Rollback — is that integrated with our infra? We prefer automatic rollback for regressions.
[04:41] Priya Nair: For Dedicated and Private yes, Canary policies can call your webhook or trigger internal rollback. Hosted has built-in fallback variants.
[04:53] Lena Cho: On metrics — can we capture domain-specific metrics? Like medical hallucination rate?
[04:59] Priya Nair: Yes you can add custom metrics via taggers or provide a rubric; we support human-in-the-loop labeling through the console or APIs to build up ground truth.
[05:13] Jordan Lee: We'll demo a pairwise chart — here's a precision-like metric and a safety score over time. You can overlay A/B runs and filter by prompt category.
[05:28] [screen share pauses briefly] Priya Nair: Jumping ahead to an example alert — this one tripped a regression on 'diagnostic safety' after a model bump. The alert page includes sample diffs, failing prompts, and an option to create a ticket.
[05:47] Samir Kapoor: How do you avoid alert thrash? We need consolidated owner assignments, not fifty small emails.
[05:53] Priya Nair: You can group alerts and set escalation policies; also silence windows and aggregated summaries. Many customers tie alerts into pager duty for critical regressions.
[06:06] Marta Ruiz: Security — we need SOC2 report, network architecture diagram, and a data flow map for PII handling.
[06:13] Jordan Lee: We'll send the SOC2 and a network diagram. For PII, we offer redaction pipelines and configurable retention. We'll attach a short whitepaper on how logs are manipulated.
[06:26] Lena Cho: In your Optimize tab, you mentioned quantization recs — can you show that?
[06:31] Priya Nair: Yep, Optimize analyzes token distribution and suggests quantization profiles per model+workload; it also simulates cost/latency tradeoffs. For Helix we might recommend 4-bit quant on long-diagnosis prompts but FP16 for short-context critical outputs.
[06:49] Samir Kapoor: Can Optimize enforce model gating in prod? Like block a quantized variant if a metric drops.
[06:54] Priya Nair: You can set quality gates tied to alerts. If a gate fails, traffic routing can be halted or routed to a safe variant.
[07:05] Jordan Lee: Quick interjection — some folks ask about competitor lock-in: Redwood supports multiple model backends and can route to vendor endpoints as a fallback.
[07:15] Marta Ruiz: Who often uses the console — ML folks or product managers?
[07:19] Priya Nair: Both. We try to make dashboards accessible to PMs while letting SEs dig into the API and raw diffs.
[07:28] Lena Cho: Can we integrate with our existing W&B for experiment tracking?
[07:32] Priya Nair: We have connectors; some customers push eval metadata into W&B or Snowflake.
[07:41] Samir Kapoor: For the A/B bench you proposed — what would the deliverables be?
[07:46] Jordan Lee: Deliverables: 24–72h benchmark run results, cost/latency breakdown, regression heatmap, and a recommendation doc for pilot configuration.
[07:58] Marta Ruiz: Ok good. Also timeline — we want pilot in November, tight compliance gating in between.
[08:04] Jordan Lee: Yep aiming for POC kickoff the week of Nov 3rd as discussed.
[08:10] [Small crosstalk] Lena Cho: Do you have an on-prem option?
[08:13] Priya Nair: Yes, Redwood Private can be deployed in-customer VPC or on-prem; includes local control plane for closed environments. There are extra steps for validation and support but it's a known path.
[08:28] Samir Kapoor: A slightly nerdy question — how do you compute pairwise significance?
[08:33] Priya Nair: We use bootstrap resampling for distributional diffs and report p-values and confidence intervals; also we support effect-size thresholds. You can export raw results for internal stats teams.
[08:46] Jordan Lee: Let's flip to a live API example — I'll post a request against the eval endpoint with a prompt-set payload.
[08:55] [typing sounds] Jordan Lee: Posting now — payload includes 200 prompts, expected label and metric script. Response comes back with scored outputs and a Delta summary.
[09:14] Marta Ruiz: Response time looks fine — what's the size of that run?
[09:17] Priya Nair: That was a small sample run; full runs can be chunked and batched. We'll run your larger sample in the bench.
[09:26] Lena Cho: If we run the bench, can we keep all telemetry in our project?
[09:30] Priya Nair: For Private yes. For Dedicated we can route telemetry to a customer-owned S3 or Snowflake. For Hosted, retention defaults are configurable and PII masking is available.
[09:42] Samir Kapoor: On cost projections, any ballpark for 1M tokens per month mixed workload?
[09:48] Jordan Lee: Depends on model and quantization but expect broad ranges in the pricing sheet I'll share — roughly $X–$Y per million for hosted, lower for Dedicated commissioning. We'll send ranges tailored to Helix after the bench.
[10:03] Marta Ruiz: Ok, let's talk about stakeholder alignment — who from Redwood will be the technical owner during the POC?
[10:08] Jordan Lee: Priya will lead the SE work and I'll coordinate commercial/contract.
[10:12] Priya Nair: I'll set up the bench, share API keys, and run the A/B with your sample traffic.
[10:19] Lena Cho: Any gotchas for medical domain prompting? We do need strong guardrails.
[10:24] Priya Nair: We recommend layered guardrails: prompt engineering, safety models, output post-processing, and human-in-loop for higher-risk outputs. The eval suite can flag safety regressions and route outputs for review.
[10:38] Jordan Lee: Wrapping toward the end — let's recap next steps. Priya will spin up the benchmark, Jordan will send pricing and security docs, Samir will drop sample traffic and retention policy.
[10:51] Samir Kapoor: Will do. One more: can you show the raw diff view?
[10:55] Priya Nair: Sure opening raw diffs — you'll see side-by-side outputs, token-level highlights, and auto-extracted failure reasons. Sometimes transcriptions of labels can look wrong, e.g., 'medicla' instead of medical in the UI if OCR picks it up, but the underlying data is intact.
[11:17] Marta Ruiz: That's helpful. If we like the bench results what are the steps to convert to a pilot?
[11:23] Jordan Lee: We'll propose a pilot SOW — typically 3 months dedicated capacity with defined success metrics and an SLA.
[11:30] Lena Cho: Price is still TBD.
[11:32] Jordan Lee: Yes, we'll include options: hosted trial, short-term dedicated reservation, or Private evaluation.
[11:40] [background noise] Samir Kapoor: For auditing, how granular are logs? We need per-request headers, model version, env id.
[11:48] Priya Nair: We log request metadata, model variant, routing decision, and an immutable audit trail for Dedicated/Private. Hosted has log views and export.
[12:02] Jordan Lee: Final question from me — any blockers from Helix side to run the bench this week?
[12:07] Marta Ruiz: We need internal signoff on data sharing but Samir will provide a sanitized profile. If he sends that by Friday you're good.
[12:15] Samir Kapoor: Will do.
[12:17] Jordan Lee: Great — thanks all. We'll follow up with notes and the links.
[12:22] [call ends]
topics: Dedicated vs Hosted vs Private deployment considerations
